text:
alex: heads-up — hit a nasty one while converting the example chat app to an edge ESM bundle. TS inference for our SDK27s generate helper just collapses at consumer build time.

alex: minimal consumer sample (Vite + esbuild target: 'esnext'):
```ts
// src/edge-client.ts
import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference'
const client = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY })
const res = await client.generate<{ text: string }>({ model: 'redwood-1', input: 'hello' })
console.log(res.text)
```

alex: compiler error in downstream: "No overload matches this call. Candidate overloads give conflicting inference for type parameter T."

mira: hmm that screams overload resolution + import shape. our typedefs currently have both a default-export-style function and a namespace-style overload for CommonJS. bundlers sometimes rewrite `import { createClient } from` into different shapes and TS picks the wrong signature.

sam: temporary unblock for users: either set `esModuleInterop: true` or import using `import * as RI from '@redwood/inference'` then `RI.createClient(...)`. I know, not great.

jin: another angle: consumers using strict "moduleResolution: bundler" + "allowSyntheticDefaultImports: false" will see the ESM import as an uncallable namespace. We should document recommended tsconfig bits for edge targets in our examples.

mira: long-term fix: collapse overloads into a single generic API surface so inference doesn't depend on overload ordering. Example change:
```ts
// types/index.d.ts (proposal)
export interface GenerateRequest<T = unknown> { model: string; input: string }
export function generate<T = unknown>(req: GenerateRequest<T>): Promise<T>
export function createClient(opts?: { apiKey?: string }): { generate: typeof generate }
export default createClient
```
This avoids CJS vs ESM dual-signature tricks and keeps inference stable.

alex: also noticed our package.json in dist has both "main" and "module" but the emitted .d.ts assumes default export in one place and named exports elsewhere. we should ship a single consistent .d.ts that matches both entry points or add a tiny compatibility shim `.default` export for CJS.

sam: can we also set "skipLibCheck": true in our published tsconfig for consumers? that reduces friction but feels like a bandaid. I prefer fixing the root types.

jin: agreed. follow-ups: 1) update types to single generic signature, 2) add a short note in edge/sample README with tsconfig recommendations (esModuleInterop true OR import * as ...), 3) add a test using Vite/esbuild target to catch regressions.

alex: i'll open a PR with the types change + update the sample app. will include a tiny repro repo and CI check that builds the sample with moduleResolution=bundler.

devex-bot: created issue #3501 (dx: edge ESM build causes generic inference failure for SDK)

mira: thanks alex. ping when PR is up and i'll review. :thumbsup:
